## Approved Spec
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-01-faelligkeitsdatum-design.md`

# Design: Fälligkeitsdatum für Todos

Ticket: #1 (adw/demo-todo) — „Fälligkeitsdatum für Todos": Todos sollen ein
Fälligkeitsdatum bekommen, damit man sieht, was überfällig ist — in der API
und in der Liste.

## Intent and why

Users should see at a glance which todos are overdue. The due date lives in the
JSON API (`/todos`) and is shown on the list page (`/`), with a filter for
overdue items in both.

## Goals

- Optional due date `due` on every todo: settable on create (`POST /todos`),
  changeable and removable later (`PATCH /todos/:id`, `due: null` removes it).
- Todos without a due date remain fully valid.
- `overdue` is visible in API responses and computable for filtering:
  `GET /todos?overdue=true` returns only overdue todos.
- List page shows the due date per todo, marks overdue todos, and has a
  "nur überfällige" control that shows only overdue todos.
- End-to-end tested by the agent in the running app (Playwright, per
  AGENTS.md); screenshots outside the repo.

## Non-goals

- No time-of-day or per-user timezones — "today" is the UTC calendar date.
- No UI for creating/editing todos or their due dates — the list page is
  read-only plus the filter control; changes go through the API.
- No persistence (store stays in-memory); no sorting changes.

## Constraints

- Zero dependencies, Node builtins only.
- Validation failures are `ValidationError` from `src/store.mjs` → HTTP 400.
- TDD: failing test in `test/` first.
- Every UI element tests rely on carries a `data-testid` (existing:
  `todo-list`, `todo-item`, `todo-title`).
- Page is German (`lang="de"`).

## Approaches

- **A (chosen): optional calendar date `due` (`YYYY-MM-DD` or `null`),
  `overdue` computed at read time against the UTC date.** Flips to overdue at
  UTC midnight without any write. Fits "Fälligkeitsdatum" exactly.
- **B (rejected): full timestamp with time** — wrong granularity for a due
  *date*, adds timezone complexity.
- **C (rejected): persisted `overdue` flag** — goes stale at midnight without a
  write.

## Decisions (as agreed with the user)

- `due` is a string `YYYY-MM-DD` or `null`; it must be a real calendar date,
  otherwise `ValidationError` → 400. Unknown/extra fields stay ignored as today.
- `overdue` is computed, never stored: `due !== null && !done && due < todayUTC`,
  where `todayUTC = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)` (UTC, per user).
  A todo due *today* is not overdue yet; a done todo is never overdue.
  `overdue` is included in every API todo response.
- `GET /todos?overdue=true` filters to overdue todos; `?overdue=false` or no
  param returns all; any other value → 400. (Builder's call, stated here.)
- `PATCH /todos/:id` accepts `due: "YYYY-MM-DD"` to change and `due: null` to
  remove the date.
- List page per item: title (`todo-title`), done marker as today, due date
  (`todo-due`) rendered as `TT.MM.JJJJ`, and for overdue todos an additional
  marker `todo-overdue` ("überfällig"). New control `overdue-only-toggle`
  (checkbox, label "nur überfällige"): when checked, only overdue todos are
  rendered.

## Left to the builder

- Calendar-date validation (regex + round-trip through `Date`).
- Where exactly `overdue` is attached (store read methods), keeping tests
  deterministic with clearly past/future dates (e.g. `2000-01-01`,
  `2999-12-31`).
- Implementation of the `?overdue=` query handling in `src/app.mjs`.
- Minimal styling for the overdue marker; rendering + toggle logic in
  `public/index.html`.
- Tests in `test/app.test.mjs` (TDD) covering: create with/without due,
  invalid due → 400, PATCH change/remove, done todo never overdue,
  `?overdue=true/false/garbage`, list page contains the new testids.

## End-to-end (agreed scope)

The agent tests end-to-end itself: start `PORT=3000 npm start &`, wait for
`/health`, seed todos via the API (overdue, future, no date, done+overdue),
verify in the browser via Playwright that the list shows dates (`TT.MM.JJJJ`),
marks only the overdue one, and that "nur überfällige" shows only that one;
screenshots outside the repo; then stop the app.

## Implementation Summary

**Approach** — Optional due date per todo, per the approved spec: `src/store.mjs` validates `due` (real `YYYY-MM-DD` calendar date via regex + `Date.UTC` round-trip; `null` allowed) on `POST /todos` and `PATCH /todos/:id`, and attaches a computed `overdue` flag to every API todo (`due < today-UTC && !done`; injectable clock `createStore(now)` keeps tests deterministic). `src/app.mjs` adds `GET /todos?overdue=true|false` (any other value → 400). `public/index.html` renders the date as `TT.MM.JJJJ` (`todo-due`), an "überfällig" marker (`todo-overdue`), and a "nur überfällige" checkbox (`overdue-only-toggle`). TDD throughout: 15 tests, all green.

**Consequences** — API: todo responses are now `{id, title, done, due, overdue}` (additive; `due` defaults to `null`). `POST /todos` accepts `due`; `PATCH /todos/:id` accepts `due` (string, or `null` to remove it). New `overdue` query param on `GET /todos`. UI: list shows due dates, marks overdue items, and the toggle filters the rendered list. No persistence, no other endpoints changed.

**Possible side effects** — API consumers see two new additive fields (backward compatible). `overdue` flips at UTC midnight without any write. Pre-existing wart left untouched (out of scope): a rejected PATCH (400) can still apply earlier valid fields, e.g. `{done:true, due:"garbage"}`.

**Watch when testing** — Invalid dates (`2026-02-30`, `2027-02-29`, `2026-1-1`) → 400; leap day `2028-02-29` → ok. Due today (UTC) is not overdue; due yesterday is; a done todo is never overdue. `?overdue=banana` → 400; `PATCH {due:null}` clears the date. End-to-end status: tested by the agent in the running app (PORT=3000, Playwright) — 4 seeded todos render with `TT.MM.JJJJ` dates, exactly the overdue one is marked, the toggle narrows the list to 1 item and back to 4; API filter verified via HTTP. Evidence (screenshots, outside the repo): /tmp/ticket1-e2e/ticket1-list.png, /tmp/ticket1-e2e/ticket1-overdue-only.png.
